preserved_work: Retained the preceding native monotonic process-start observation and fresh psutil.Process(pid) PID-reuse comparison.
Removed only the dead psutil.boot_time monkeypatch from the split-UID test; the unrelated repair1 report remains untouched and unstaged.
changed_contracts: Linux boot_identity continues to use the validated kernel boot_id.

Darwin boot_identity now reads only a bounded kern.bootsessionuuid through native sysctlbyname, validates an exact UUID, and returns state-unavailable for syscall, unavailable, malformed, overlong, or unexpected data.

process_identity continues to use psutil 7.2.2's private native create_time(monotonic=True), which is a kernel start stamp: boot-relative on Linux and a raw start-time stamp on macOS. The value is equality-only within one boot identity; a psutil pin upgrade requires revalidating this private contract.
Process exit races during the second psutil.Process(pid) observation or os.getpgid(pid) return no identity.
negative_contracts: Darwin wall-clock changes cannot change a live boot identity and psutil.boot_time is never used.
Unavailable or invalid native observations fail closed without argv, command-line, environment, domain-state, or signal side effects.
A reused PID or either specified exit race returns None.
